Why is it that the majority of people who get sickle cell anemia are of African descent?

There's some proof that sickle cell anemia protects against the parasite that causes malaria. Malaria happens to be spread in tropical areas - of which Africa has plenty.
Over countless generations, the populous has naturally selected for that feature to be present.
Did you get all that Timmy?
It should be added though that the cells do not protect against the parasite that gives you malaria, but due to the inefficiency of sickle cell anemia, the infection itself has trouble mobilizing

The extremely simplified answer is that sickle cell traits somehow protect babies against malaria and is therefore an advantage for survival so long as the sickle cell traits aren't so pronounced that they themselves become a cause of death.

http://www.cdc.gov/malaria/about/biology/sickle_cell.html

It is from a recessive genetic trait that originated in populations in West Africa. Only if both parents pass on the trait will the child develop the severely deformed red blood cells that define the condition. If the child only inherits the gene from one parent, the red blood cells are only slightly deformed, but do not present any anemic symptoms. The condition is generally thought to be mildly protective against malaria, where the slightly deformed blood cells are less readily consumed by the parasite while not being deformed enough to cause anemia.
